questions.prompt: A string has length \(0.90\,\mathrm{m}\). Find the wavelength of its fundamental mode.
If the fundamental frequency of a string is \(110\,\mathrm{Hz}\), what is the second-harmonic frequency?
A string supports waves at \(150\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}\) and has length \(0.75\,\mathrm{m}\). Find the third-harmonic frequency.
How many interior nodes does the \(n=5\) mode of a string fixed at both ends have?
questions.answer:
Mode \(n\) has \(n-1\) interior nodes, so the \(n=5\) mode has
\[
5-1=4
\]
interior nodes.

questions.prompt: A string has \(f_1=80\,\mathrm{Hz}\). A standing wave is observed at \(320\,\mathrm{Hz}\). What mode number is this?
questions.answer:
Use
\[
f_n=nf_1
\]
so
\[
n=\frac{f_n}{f_1}=\frac{320}{80}=4
\]
It is the fourth mode.

questions.prompt: Two strings carry waves at the same speed. String B is twice as long as string A. Compare their fundamental frequencies.
questions.answer:
The fundamental is
\[
f_1=\frac{v_w}{2L}
\]
If string B has twice the length, then
\[
f_{1,B}=\frac{v_w}{2(2L_A)}=\frac{1}{2}\frac{v_w}{2L_A}=\frac{f_{1,A}}{2}
\]
So string B has half the fundamental frequency of string A.

questions.prompt: String A has length \(L\) and string B has length \(2L\). The wave speed is the same in both strings. Find a pair of nonzero mode numbers \((n_A,n_B)\) for which the two strings can share the same normal-mode frequency.
questions.answer:
Equal frequencies require
\[
\frac{n_Av}{2L}=\frac{n_Bv}{2(2L)}
\]
Cancel \(v\) and simplify:
\[
\frac{n_A}{L}=\frac{n_B}{2L}
\quad\Rightarrow\quad
n_B=2n_A
\]
One simple nonzero pair is
\[
(n_A,n_B)=(1,2)
\]
More generally, any pair with \(n_B=2n_A\) works.

questions.prompt: Two strings have lengths \(L_A\) and \(L_B\) and wave speeds \(v_A\) and \(v_B\). Derive the condition relating mode numbers \(n_A\) and \(n_B\) for the two strings to have equal normal-mode frequencies.
questions.answer:
The normal-mode frequencies are
\[
f_{n_A}=\frac{n_Av_A}{2L_A},
\qquad
f_{n_B}=\frac{n_Bv_B}{2L_B}
\]
For them to be equal,
\[
\frac{n_Av_A}{2L_A}=\frac{n_Bv_B}{2L_B}
\]
so the condition is
\[
\frac{n_Av_A}{L_A}=\frac{n_Bv_B}{L_B}
\]
or equivalently
\[
n_Av_AL_B=n_Bv_BL_A
\]
That is the required relation between the two mode numbers.
